title: India’s steel output rises 3.6% in October, but global production dips - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
India retained its position as the world’s second-largest crude steel producer, behind China

India’s crude steel production rose 3.6 per cent year-on-year to 14.5 million tonnes (mt) in October 2026, even as global output declined 1.1 per cent to 142.4 mt, according to the latest data released by the World Steel Association (worldsteel).

India retained its position as the world’s second-largest crude steel producer, behind China, which recorded a 1.6 per cent decline in production to 70.8 mt during the month.

India’s cumulative crude steel production during January-October 2026 increased 5.2 per cent to 144.1 mt against 2025, reflecting continued growth in domestic steel production.

China’s output during the first 10 months, however, declined 2.8 per cent to 795.6 mt.

Global crude steel production across the 70 countries reporting to worldsteel stood at 142.4 mt in October, down 1.1 per cent from 143.9 mt in the year-ago period.

Cumulative production during January-October 2026 fell 0.8 per cent to 1,509.3 mt. The 70 countries covered by the data accounted for approximately 98 per cent of global crude steel production in 2025.

Among other major producers, the US recorded an estimated 8.4 per cent increase in output to 7.5 mt in October. Japan’s production declined 2.3 per cent to 6.7 mt, while Russia’s estimated output rose 1.9 per cent to 5.4 mt.

South Korea produced 5.3 mt, up 3.7 per cent, while Turkiye’s output increased 5.5 per cent to 3.4 mt. Germany’s production declined 9.6 per cent to 2.8 mt. Brazil also recorded a 5.4 per cent decline to 2.8 mt.

Vietnam emerged as the fastest-growing producer among the top 10 countries, with output surging 28.5 per cent to 2.7 mt in October.

Among the major steel-producing regions, Asia and Oceania recorded production of 102.7 mt in October, unchanged from the year-ago period.

The European Union’s (27 countries) output declined 4 per cent to 10.5 mt, while West Asia recorded the steepest regional contraction, with production falling 27.7 per cent to 3.9 mt.

North America registered a 5.6 per cent increase to 9.7 mt, while Africa’s output rose 7.9 per cent to 2.1 mt. Production in Europe outside the EU increased 5.1 per cent to 3.8 mt.

South America’s output declined 4.1 per cent to 3.6 mt, while Russia and other CIS countries, along with Ukraine, recorded a 6.8 per cent decline to 6 mt.
